symptom: `describe import mapping M.X` / `describe export mapping M.X` reports "not found" for a mapping that exists and that `show` lists. `create or modify json structure` silently creates a duplicate instead of modifying the existing one. All of them work if the document happens to sit directly under the module rather than in a folder
cause: `Backend.moduleNameFor` resolved a unit's module by reading its **direct** container (`GetModule(u.ContainerID)`). Studio Pro nests documents in folders — and folders in folders — so for any foldered document the container is a `Projects$Folder`, `GetModule` returns nil, the name resolves to `""`, and every `…ByQualifiedName` lookup built on it misses. In a stock marketplace project this is the *normal* case, not an edge case: 15 of 16 microflows, both JSON structures and both mappings were foldered, while all 8 domain models sat directly under their module — which is exactly why the three domain-model callers worked and hid the defect
insight: Walk the containment chain to the first enclosing module instead of reading one level. Build the parent map once (the old code re-scanned `ListUnits()` per call, inside a loop over every document — O(n²)), and **guard the walk against cycles**: the project root is its own container, so an unguarded loop hangs. Behaviour is unchanged for direct children, so the domain-model callers are unaffected. **Generalisable — the shape to look for**: a containment lookup that reads one level where the model allows arbitrary nesting. It works on every fixture built by `create module` + `create X` (nothing is foldered) and fails on every real project, so unit tests pass while users see "not found". **Diagnostic trap**: `describeImportMapping` wraps any error containing "not found" in `mdlerrors.NewNotFound`, so the surfaced message is identical whichever layer failed and cannot be used to identify the engine — call the reader and the backend directly to tell them apart. The legacy `sdk/mpr` reader walks the chain correctly (`buildContainerModuleNameMap`), so **the two engines disagreed** and only the default (modelsdk) was broken. Test `mdl/backend/modelsdk/module_resolution_test.go`
